Cc: FinTrust Security Team <security@fintrust.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CAIQ coverage + evidence request for FinTrust audit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. FinTrust is preparing for an external review in early August and we need a CAIQ-style mapping from Redwood that shows which Cloud Controls (CSA/CAIQ) your platform asserts and the specific artifacts that substantiate each assertion.

Deliverables we need: a compact spreadsheet mapping Control IDs -> Redwood assertions -> artifact filename or link, a short narrative for any partial/no coverage controls, and an evidence bundle (or instructions for secure access) for reviewers. Attached is our request form that lists the scope and a sample CAIQ we use.

Key dates: please confirm a delivery plan by July 2 and a complete package by July 9 if possible. Also would like a 30–45 minute walkthrough the week of July 5.

Attachment: FinTrust_CA_Request.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate your help — the auditor (BlueWave) will want traceability down to log samples and configuration docs.

Heather Cho
Security Manager, FinTrust Bank
heather@fintrust.com

Hi Heather — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We're ready to support the review and propose the following plan: 

1) Deliverable set by July 7: a compact mapping spreadsheet (ControlID, Redwood assertion, evidence pointer, owner, notes) + a one-page narrative for any controls with partial coverage.
2) Evidence package uploaded to a secure share by July 9 (or we can provide a curated zip for the auditor).
3) Walkthrough: 30-minute call on July 6 or 7 (please let us know a preferred slot).

I'll attach an initial mapping workbook (work-in-progress) and Sean will follow up with the evidence index and owner roster. Kimberly will coordinate any redaction/PII gating for logs.

Attachment: redwood_caiq_mapping_v0.xlsx (xlsx)

Next steps: we'll send the evidence index and a proposed call time later today.

Best,

Hi all,

Quick technical note on format and traceability so the auditor can follow artifacts end-to-end: our mapping uses a simple column schema (ControlID, Assertion, ArtifactType, ArtifactPath, EvidenceOwner, SampleDate). The ArtifactPath will either be a secure link (shared with BlueWave) or an internal reference that we export into the evidence-index zip.

For logs we will provide sample slices (redacted) that show retention windows and relevant events. For KMS/keys, we will provide rotation policy and a signed statement from our infrastructure team documenting KMS usage patterns and HSM/KMS provider details.

I attached an evidence-index bundle with pointers and a manifest so BlueWave can request specific artifacts. We can also provide a short README that maps the column names to CAIQ control identifiers.

Attachment: evidence-index.zip (zip)

Heather / team — a couple of practical notes from the evidence-prep side: 

- Redaction and PII: we'll provide log slices with IP and user identifiers redacted; where redaction would remove substantive context we will instead provide sanitized reproductions and an explanation column in the mapping.
- Access model: we prefer to stage artifacts on a time-limited secure share (pre-authenticated links) for the auditor; if BlueWave requires direct download, we can produce a curated zip.
- Expected artifacts: SOC2-Attestation.pdf, kms-rotation-policy.pdf, runtime-telemetry-sample.log (redacted), infra-configs.tar.gz (config snapshots). We'll include an artifact-manifest.csv that maps each file to control IDs and the person responsible for follow-up.

If you have any specific extraction requirements for BlueWave (e.g., MD5 checksums or signed attestations), flag that and we will add it to the manifest.

Attachment: artifact-manifest.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
kimberly_park@redwood.com
